It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the "unsearchable riches" of Christ while observing a world that seeks to "remodel the way we think about truth" by borrowing moral language from the Bible while rejecting the King, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the world's search for wisdom? [13, 23, 1395, 1503, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling "overwhelmed and desperate" by those who use Jesus’ name to "justify sin," or are you seeking a "settled certainty" in the "spotless purity of truth" that cannot be found in mere human "philanthropy"? [20, 1076, 1393, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many "shave off the edges" of the truth to find "common ground" with those who "suppress the truth in unrighteousness," we must return to the "external Word" to see how the Lord personally governs the "vicissitudes of life" by demanding that we "worship Him in spirit and truth" (John 4:24) [11, 28, 654, 1073, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that "God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation," and therefore, the world's attempts to separate "moral wisdom" from "divine authority" is not an "administrative anomaly" but evidence of a "rebellious heart" that God uses to prove that "His counsel shall stand, and He will do all His pleasure" (Isaiah 46:10) [15, 68, 1143, 1460, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: Seeking Moral Wisdom without Divine Authority**

**Verse**
“Because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God, nor were thankful, but became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish hearts were darkened. Professing to be wise, they became fools” (Romans 1:21–22). [1073, 1359, 1714, 1715, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that the world attempts to "take the parts of Jesus they like" (His humanity or kindness) while rejecting Him as "God our creator" [1078, 1080, Conversation History]. Secular leaders often use the words of Christ on "billboards" to "argue for their sins," yet they remain "alienated and hostile in mind" because they refuse His Lordship [1076, 1078, 1079, Conversation History]. When a culture seeks "moral wisdom" without recognizing the "Master and Owner," they are merely "exchanging the truth of God for a lie," for "the carnal mind is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can be" (Romans 8:7; Romans 1:25) [43, 1134, 1405, 1500, 1715, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by those who admire Jesus as a "good teacher" but ignore His "binding and authoritative mandate," for "your life is not your own" because you were "bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 91, 101, 1078, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge," and any morality that starts with "human ingenuity" rather than "trembling at My word" will "vanish—like smoke they vanish away" (Proverbs 1:7; Isaiah 66:2; Psalm 102:3) [11, 21, 32, 1143, 1313, 1373, 1411, 1503, 1684, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the "religious aristocracy" was "punctilious" about "legal minutiae" like "gnat straining," yet they "neglected the weightier matters" of "justice and mercy" (Matthew 23:23–24) [8, 176, 177, 1091, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that even the most "highly religious culture" is "hard-hearted" if it "despises wisdom and instruction," for "it is written: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent'" (1 Corinthians 1:19; Proverbs 1:7) [191, 1407, 1424, 1531, 1575, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Common Grace vs. Saving Faith in Public Ethics**

**Verse**
“that you may be sons of your Father in heaven; for He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust” (Matthew 5:45). [65, 1143, 1381, 1160, 1161, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture teaches that God provides "temporal blessings" and "providential care" to all of "mankind" through "common grace," even to those who "blaspheme His name" [65, 1095, 1114, 1143, 1381, Conversation History]. While we are commanded to be "loyal and submissive" to governments that provide "civil peace," these ethical "methods and programs" must not be confused with "divine blessing" or "salvation," for "every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father" (James 1:17) [3, 93, 147, 229, 1201, 1339, Conversation History]. The church’s "chief mission" is not to "legislate morality" but to lead people to a "saving knowledge," for "Jesus answered, 'My kingdom is not of this world' ” (John 18:36) [27, 28, 29, 1592, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Never become so involved in this world" that you seek "deliverance" through "political maneuvering and lobbying" rather than the "gospel of the grace of God" (Acts 20:24) [27, 51, 93, 130, 843, 1020, 1503, 1623, Conversation History]. You should "discipline your mind" to recognize that "righteousness exalts a nation," yet only "the Holy Spirit and the Spirit-inspired Scriptures" can "make you wise for salvation" (Proverbs 14:34; 2 Timothy 3:15) [30, 116, 145, 1503, 1532, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "national greatness" and "large cities" were "temporal signs" of God's favor for His "theocratic people" [409, 1353, 1386, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by revealing that we are "sojourners and pilgrims" whose "citizenship is in heaven," and our "victory" is found not in "carnal weaponry" or ethical legislation, but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” (Revelation 12:11; Philippians 3:20) [13, 21, 26, 32, 92, 142, 440, 1020, 1313, 1426, 1515, 1646, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Insufficiency of Moralism without Regeneration**

**Verse**
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs which indeed appear beautiful outwardly, but inside are full of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness. Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness” (Matthew 23:27–28). [122, 1347, 1472, 1486, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—upheld by **John MacArthur**—asserts that "performative religion" and "moralism" are "spiritual placebos" that mask a heart "dead in trespasses and sins" [20, 122, 146, 250, 1486, Conversation History]. A "profession of faith" or an "outward display of piety" is no "proof of genuine conversion" if the life is not "transformed," for "as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also" (James 2:26) [408, 471, 1399, 1478, Conversation History]. Sinners may "ape the world’s fads" of "altruism" or "humanitarianism," but these "filthy rags" cannot "merit heaven," for "all of us have become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a filthy garment" (Isaiah 64:6) [11, 16, 206, 247, 264, 1213, 1315, 1491, 1617, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must "confess your own utter spiritual poverty," for "the gospel has nothing to say to people who are satisfied with their own righteousness" [11, 61, 153, 207, 233, 262, 1169, 1403, Conversation History]. Recognize that "the saved know they are wicked" while "the damned think they are good," and your "sole objective" is to find "rest" in Christ's "finished work" (John 19:30; Matthew 11:28) [24, 101, 277, 1099, 1132, 1406, 1445, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "man-made representations" and "ritualized ceremonies" were "shadows" intended to "reveal sin" [13, 1391, 1432, 1482, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that "everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ," and we now offer a "living sacrifice" through the "renewing of your mind" (Romans 12:1; Hebrews 4:10) [13, 17, 24, 136, 142, 157, 446, 860, 1101, 1212, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Miracle of the New Birth**

**Verse**
“Jesus answered and said to him, ‘Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God’ ” (John 3:3). [597, 598, 599, 600, 604, 805, 873, 1206, 1314, 1456, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that "salvation is a supernatural work of God" where the Spirit "imparts life to dead hearts" [11, 251, 339, 429, 803, 822, 1091, Conversation History]. Regeneration is not a "conscious choice" born of "human effort" or moral self-improvement, but a "miracle" that occurs "not by the will of the flesh... but of God" (John 1:13) [11, 15, 251, 427, 615, 1091, 1331, 1503, Conversation History]. Because we were "born radically depraved and god-hating," only "the washing of regeneration" can "transform our nature" so we may "yield unconditionally to Christ" [138, 145, 254, 332, 339, 417, 601, 804, 1212, 1318, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Trade in your worry for trust," for "He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6) [5, 94, 201, 829, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your body and bring it into subjection," finding "joy, satisfaction, [and] contentment" solely in the "Spirit-inspired Scriptures" that "guide you into all truth" (John 16:13; 1 Corinthians 9:27) [13, 20, 79, 110, 116, 1311, 1406, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: The Jews had picked up this practice from the Gentiles, who believed that the value of prayer was largely a matter of quantity, supposing “they [would] be heard for their many words.” They believed their deities first had to be aroused, then cajoled, intimidated, and finally badgered into listening and answering. Prayer was simply a matter of religious ceremony to the Gentiles, and it became that way for the Jews as well. Since no effort is required in those types of prayer, those who followed that practice could be totally indifferent to the prayer’s content. But worse than that, they were indifferent to real communion with God.

The ability to think clearly and correctly is a tremendous blessing from God. It all begins with the gospel, which is “the power of God for salvation” (Rom. 1:16). The Lord uses the gospel to illumine the mind of the unbeliever. In fact, Paul said that faith comes by hearing about Christ (Rom. 10:17). Salvation begins in the mind as an individual comes to realize the seriousness of sin and Christ’s atoning work on his or her behalf. Jesus said, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind” (Luke 10:27). Salvation requires an intelligent response: trust in the revealed truth of God, which proves itself in life to be true and reasonable.

Jamie  November 5, 2014 Reply I’m not sure that it’s fair to say with such a sweeping statement that there is anti-intellectualism and a distaste of biblical doctrines in the charismatic movement. In my world, there seems to be a bit of a distaste for the dispensationist-leaning doctrines that deny these gifts; I wouldn’t say that they dislike doctrine. They hold firmly to doctrine; it’s just different doctrine than the likes of MacArthur hold, and because of a different way of interpreting and harmonizing the texts. And the anti-intellectual label is an unfortunate over-simplifying of the issue. I believe there is a tension between what the scriptures seem to present as truth and what our experience does not always confirm; and I think that it might be fair to say (not trying to insult, but to simplify to illustrate the difference, and perhaps painting with a broad brush in the process) that some will try to live with a tension between what they believe the word says and what they’ve not yet seen manifest in their walks; others will find ways to moderate their expectations as a way to explain why the things they think they would perhaps like to see do not always happen. But once you’ve experienced firsthand some of these things happening in your own world, in response to your own prayers of expectation and the healings that result, you’re kind of forced to have to re-evaluate your doctrine. I believe this is what the charismatics are trying to do. And yes, there are abuses. But that is not the the litmus test for whether or not it’s true.

That also explains why worldly people don’t understand or appreciate why Christians are passionate about the glory of God. They don’t understand why we prize the kingdom of heaven so highly when it means nothing to them. Unregenerate people simply have no sense of what divine glory entails. They can’t fathom why someone would willingly submit to the lordship of Jesus Christ. They don’t understand why anyone would repudiate sin and its pleasures in order to pursue righteousness, sacrificing earthly delights for heavenly joys. That goes against every instinct and every desire of the fallen human heart.

People who protest that God is unfair or unjust when He shows grace to the least deserving people simply do not understand the principle of grace. Undiluted justice would mean immediate death for every sinner, because “the wages of sin is death” (Rom. 6:23). The truth is, we don’t really want what is “fair.” We all desperately need grace and mercy. On the other hand, grace is not unjust, because Christ made full atonement for the sins of those who trust Him—and thereby turned justice in their favor. “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9, emphasis added). Because Christ took the penalty of sin on Himself, God can justify believing sinners (even notorious sinners like the thief on the cross) without compromising His own righteousness. “He [is both] just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus” (Rom. 3:26).

In other words, what we do with our money reveals the true state of our heart. Therefore, “If you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?” (Luke 16:11). Those who are not investing in the work of redemption are shirking their duty to be faithful stewards, wasting this passing moment of opportunity, and impoverishing themselves in eternity. God doesn’t reward people for frittering away His resources. To spend money on unnecessary luxuries and status symbols—or even cheap trinkets, trifles, creature comforts, and worthless, time-wasting diversions—is to rob oneself of true, eternal riches.

No miracle of any magnitude will convince someone who hears and understands the message of Scripture but rejects it anyway. Only the Holy Spirit can open blind eyes and melt hardened hearts to receive the Word. And the truth of God’s Word is the only message with the power to save. If you reject the Word of God but believe in some miracle, religious experience, or private revelation, your faith is not saving faith at all. And those the Word of God will be judged by the very truth they reject. In John 12:46–48 Jesus said, “I have come as a light into the world, that whoever believes in Me should not abide in darkness. And if anyone hears My words and does not believe, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world. He who rejects Me, and does not receive My words, has that which judges him—the word that I have spoken will judge him in the last day.”

All of them have positioned themselves as role models for the young restless and reformed, and yet the charge they are making betrays an appalling ignorance of the historic reformed emphasis on the doctrine of divine providence. Their accusation against non-Charismatics is rooted in their own failure to appreciate what Scripture teaches about the imminence of God, that God personally and constantly and permanently and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation. God is personally present and meticulously at work in everything that happens, even when He is not manifesting His presence by miracles. That's what I believe. I am not a skeptic who refuses to see God's hand at work in Christians lives. I just want to preserve a biblical sense of sanity in the claims we make about how God works and what it means when He does. And that's the doctrine of providence. And I want to explore this subject with you in this session, starting in Matthew 10...Matthew 10.
